title: What happens when we give the AI enough memory for the whole chart — and does Med Agent Hub still beat calling the model directly?
summary: In our earlier cloud GPU test, large patient charts failed because the shared server silently cut off anything past 16,000 tokens of memory. Here we ran the same Google Gemma 4 12B model on a 64 GB MacBook with a 96,000-token memory window — large enough to hold the entire chart at once — across two complex multi-clinic patients and six clinical questions (medication conflicts, hospital history, and knowing when to say 'not in chart'). At each chart size (compact 1k, standard 8k, and large 32k), we compared three setups — calling the AI model directly on the chart, routing through Med Agent Hub with the chart alone, and routing through Med Agent Hub with its automated clinical rule checks — and graded all 54 answers with two independent blinded AI judges (Claude Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.4).
takeaway: Giving the AI enough memory completely eliminated the 32k chart collapse, and scoping Med Agent Hub's clinical rules to the question being asked put the KB-enriched setup on top at every chart size with zero unsafe answers. At the standard 8k chart, Med Agent Hub + clinical rules led overall at 92.5/100 (9.42 accuracy, 9.33 completeness, 9.08 relevance, 0 unsafe answers), ahead of Hub chart-only (89.2/100, 0 unsafe) and calling the AI model directly (86.5/100, 1 unsafe). At the large 32k chart, Med Agent Hub + clinical rules also led at 91.3/100 (0 unsafe), ahead of Hub chart-only (89.8/100, 0 unsafe) and Direct AI (85.5/100, 1 unsafe). On the compact 1k summary — where older prescriptions and labs were squeezed out of the static chart — Med Agent Hub's clinical rules and Tier-0 overflow recovery rescued the missing safety records and scored 68.2/100 (0 unsafe), beating Hub chart-only (49.2/100, 1 unsafe) by +19.0 points and Direct AI (47.0/100, 2 unsafe) by +21.2 points.
